hero.name: Kevin
hero.subtext: We made something especially for you.
hero.cardNote: From all of us at Team Zenmonk

story.title: This isn't just another birthday card.
story.subtitle: We wanted to tell you what you've actually left behind with us.
paragraphs: When we sat down to think about what to make for your birthday, we realized a standard greeting card or a corporate message wouldn't do justice to the journey we've shared.
You haven't just managed a team or assigned roadmap deliverables. You've fundamentally shaped how we view software, how we tackle complexity, and how we collaborate every single day.
story.quote: “You taught us how to build. So we built something for you.”

legacy.heading: You taught us how to build.
legacy.subheading: Not just features. Not just applications. Systems.
legacy.leadQuote: “You didn't just teach us how to build software. You taught us how to think about building software.”

pillars.title: Domain-Driven Design
pillars.quote: “You taught us to understand the domain before rushing into the code.”
pillars.description: To listen to the domain experts, respect the boundaries, and design models that reflect real-world problem spaces rather than database schemas.

pillars.title: Software Architecture
pillars.quote: “You taught us to think about boundaries, decisions, and why systems are structured the way they are.”
pillars.description: Architectural decisions have consequences. You taught us that good structure is about isolating change and making the future easier to navigate.

pillars.title: System Design
pillars.quote: “You taught us to see the entire system, not just the feature in front of us.”
pillars.description: Looking at asynchronous event streams, state lifecycles, scalability trade-offs, and how each component fits into the grand vision.

pillars.title: Engineering Thinking
pillars.quote: “You taught us to ask 'Why?' before asking 'How?'”
pillars.description: Challenging initial assumptions, digging to the root of requirements, and making deliberate technical trade-offs with clear intent.

pillars.title: Technical Excellence
pillars.quote: “You taught us that making something work is only the beginning.”
pillars.description: Code readability, testability, domain expressiveness, and long-term maintainability are where real engineering value lives.

legacy.transitionPause1: These stopped being things you taught us.
legacy.transitionPunchline: They became the way we build.
legacy.transitionNote: A mindset forged in architectural rigor and mutual trust.

teamMessages.heading: Every great system has people behind it.
teamMessages.subheading: And every growing engineer has people who helped them get there.

paragraphs: Thank you for teaching us to look at software differently.

DDD, architecture, system design, and all the engineering principles you've shared with us have become much more than technical concepts. They have changed the way we approach problems, make decisions, and think about the systems we build.
You've pushed us to go beyond simply making things work — to understand the domain, question our decisions, think about boundaries, and care about the quality of what we create.
More importantly, you've given us the opportunity to learn, experiment, make mistakes, and grow as engineers.
Thank you for being the person who taught us not just how to build software, but how to think like engineers.
chandanLetter.author: Chandan

members.name: Satvik
members.message: Happy Birthday Kevin! Thank you for raising the bar on system design and teaching us to think deeply before writing a single line of code. Hope you have a fantastic celebration!

members.name: Harish
members.message: Wishing you the happiest birthday, Kevin! Your architectural insights and commitment to quality inspire all of us to be better engineers every day.

members.name: Team Zenmonk
members.message: From brainstorming domain events to refactoring core modules, thank you for guiding us with patience, clarity, and visionary leadership!

ctoStatus.heading: CTO SYSTEM STATUS
ctoStatus.systemStatusNote: No critical issues detected. Although the team continues to generate unexpected requirements. 😉

finalMessage.heading: But seriously...
paragraphs: A CTO doesn't just build systems.
A great leader creates an environment where people learn to build better systems themselves.

You've taught us to question assumptions. To understand the domain. To think in boundaries. To design before we implement. And to care about the systems we're building — not just the code we're writing.
finalMessage.closingLesson: Those lessons will travel much further than any project we've built together.
finalMessage.signoff: From all of us at Team Zenmonk ❤️

celebration.heading: Happy Birthday Kevin! 🎉
celebration.subheading: Wishing you an extraordinary year filled with joy, great architecture, and great adventures.
